newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares sink on dull day, more losses ahead.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares sink on dull day, more losses ahead.

text.p: Danish share prices closed lower in a dull market on Monday hit by falling bonds and low turnover, with dealers seeing the negative trend setting in.

"The main reason for the decline was the falling bond market, hitting financial paper in particular. We look like seeing more falls ahead before we bottom out ahead of the mid-August corporate interim result season," one dealer said.

The KFX top-20 index closed 2.60 point down at 186.68 in overall bourse turnover of only 693 million crowns. The KFX August future fell 4.20 point to 185.00 with 523 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
Dealers said August 13, when biotechnological group Novo Nordisk and SAS were due to issue their first-half 1997 results could be a turning point for the stock market.
SAS fell 5.7 percent or 5.7 crowns to close at 105, with Novo finishing nine crowns lower at 725.
